exposure: heterozygous novel variant in CFB (c.1101 C>A, p.Ser367Arg)
cohort: The study included two unrelated Caucasian female patients diagnosed with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome, one presenting at 10 months old and the other at 31 years old.
finding: The novel heterozygous CFB variant (p.Ser367Arg) is a gain-of-function pathogenic variant that leads to fluid-phase dysregulation of the alternative complement pathway and increased C3b deposition on cell surfaces, explaining atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome.
mod_finding: One patient presented at age 31 with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome following a caesarean section for preeclampsia.
followup_time: 31 years (for one patient, based on presentation age relative to birth)
